'''''Amaranthus albus''''' is an [[Annual plant|annual]] species of [[flowering plant]] native to the Americas. Its [[common name]]s include '''common tumbleweed''',<ref name="GRIN">{{GRIN | accessdate=20 July 2014}}</ref> '''tumble pigweed''',<ref name="GRIN" /> '''tumbleweed''',<ref name="GRIN" /> '''prostrate pigweed''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=AMAL|taxon=Amaranthus albus|accessdate=7 January 2016}}</ref> '''pigweed amaranth''', '''white amaranth'''<ref name="GRIN" /> and '''white pigweed'''.<ref name="GRIN" />

== Description ==
''Amaranthus albus'' is an [[Annual plant|annual]] herb growing up to {{Convert|50|cm}} tall, forming many branches. Larger specimens turn into [[tumbleweed]]s when they die and dry out. The plant creates small, greenish flowers in clumps in the [[axils]] of the leaves. Male and female flowers are mixed together in the same clump.<ref name="Flora of China">[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200006978 Flora of China, <big>白苋</big> bai xian ''Amaranthus albus'' Linnaeus]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200006978 Flora of North America, Tumbleweed amaranth, tumble pigweed, white amaranth''Amaranthus albus'' Linnaeus, Syst. Nat. ed. 10. 2: 1268. 1759. ]</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
It is native to the tropical Americas, but is a widespread [[introduced species]] in other places, including Europe, Africa, and Australia.<ref name="Flora of China" /><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=amaranthus+albus Altervista Flora Italiana, Amaranto bianco, weißer Fuchsschwanz, carurú-branco, ''Amaranthus albus'' L.] includes photos and European distribution map</ref><ref>[http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:385719 Atlas of Living Australia]</ref>

== Uses ==
In [[Cambodia]], the leaves of the plant (which is known as {{Lang|km-Latn|phti sâ}} in the [[Khmer language]]) are used as pig feed, and are sometimes cooked and eaten by people.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Pauline Dy Phon |title=Plants Utilised In Cambodia/Plantes utilisées au Cambodge |date=2000 |publisher=Imprimerie Olympic |location=Phnom Penh |page=121 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=InD2RAAACAAJ|author1-link=Pauline Dy Phon }}</ref>
